name: flying-island
description: Floating rounded islands with native window glass (macOS vibrancy, Windows 11 acrylic/mica) and a high-contrast dark theme built from the open-source IntelliJ Platform palette.

flyingIsland.autoApply.description: Inject the island geometry CSS into VS Code on startup (re-applies after VS Code updates).

enumDescriptions: macOS: blurred desktop behind the window (Windows: acrylic)
Windows 11: Mica, tinted wallpaper without live blur (macOS: under-window)
flyingIsland.vibrancy.description: Native translucent window material behind the title bar, tool window stripe, status bar and Project island. Requires quitting and reopening VS Code.

flyingIsland.vibrancyOpacity.description: How solid the translucent chrome is over the blur (0.3 = very glassy, 1 = opaque).

flyingIsland.gap.markdownDescription: Gap between neighbouring islands (editor groups, Project, bottom panel, chat). In pixels; applied after **Reload Window**.

flyingIsland.radius.markdownDescription: Corner radius of the islands. In pixels; applied after **Reload Window**.

flyingIsland.margin.top.markdownDescription: Space between the title bar and the top of the islands. In pixels; applied after **Reload Window**.

flyingIsland.margin.right.markdownDescription: Space between the right window edge and the rightmost island. In pixels; applied after **Reload Window**.

flyingIsland.margin.bottom.markdownDescription: Space between the bottom of the islands and the status bar (up to 6: VS Code lays out the panels itself, so a larger cut would hide their last rows). In pixels; applied after **Reload Window**.

flyingIsland.margin.left.markdownDescription: Space between the tool window stripe (activity bar) and the leftmost island. In pixels; applied after **Reload Window**.
